# The feed's tools

The tools the raea app offers every agent it launches, as the MCP server `feed` (apps/app host/acp/feed-mcp.ts).
PAGE: the feed's page answers it, so the app must be open (or a windowless page); PERSON: a click finishes it.
With no page, use the CLI instead: `raea controller` for the controllers, `raea context .` for the brief.

## feed_post

Access: PAGE.

Post an item to the project's feed: a render to watch (.mp4), a still to look at (.png/.jpg), audio to listen to (.wav/.mp3/.m4a) or a game to play (its .tsx). The person sees it in the feed and leaves notes on it; a new version of an item names the one it replaces.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required | watch, look, listen or play |
| `title` | required | what the person sees on the card |
| `file` | required | absolute path of the file to post |
| `replaces` | optional | the id of the item this is a new version of |
| `changed` | optional | with replaces: one short line on what this version changed ("title bigger, cut the second shot"); the card shows it beside the new picture |
| `export` | optional | true when this is a deliverable (an export for the client or a platform): it shows under Exports in the project's Table |
| `tags` | optional | tags; key:value tags (platform:tiktok, aspect:9x16, cut:15s, market:uk) become the Table's columns, so use the same keys across a project's exports |
| `uses` | optional | the library files it was made from (footage, stills, music) |
| `controls` | optional | play: the game's controls |

## feed_propose

Access: PAGE, then PERSON (accept).

Propose a planned item for the person to accept: what you would make next, before making it.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | required | string |
| `title` | required | the item you would make |
| `why` | optional | one line on why |

## item_tags

Access: PAGE.

Set the tags of an item already in the project's feed (feed_items lists them with their tags), to give the project's Table its structure: key:value tags (platform:tiktok, aspect:9x16) are its columns, and the tag export makes the item a deliverable. Replaces the item's own tags.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `item` | required | the item's id |
| `tags` | required | its tags, whole |

## feed_brief

Access: PAGE.

Read the project's brief as it stands now, as brief.ts (`export default brief({...})` from "raea/brief"): what to make, for whom, the one thing to believe, its deliverables and staged tasks.

No input.

## workspace_read

Access: PAGE (Chat only).

Read the workspace: its channels (id, name, logline), its agents, and its repo as raea keeps it (repo: its folder, layout, and each project's path, storage and id, from .raea/workspace). Workspace sessions (Chat) only.

No input.

## controllers_read

Access: PAGE.

Read the workspace's controllers: each controller's groups and fields with their paths (controller.group.field), types and values, as text and as JSON.

No input.

## controller_write

Access: PAGE.

Add a controller to the workspace, or replace the one with its id. A controller is { id?, title, help?, groups: [{ id?, title, help?, fields: [{ id?, label, help?, type, value, ... }] }] }; field types: toggle, choice (options), number (unit, min, max, step), text (placeholder, multiline), list, agents, channels, workflow (value: [{ name, by, back }], channels), servers, skills. The person sees it at once, and every agent works to it.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `controller` | required | the controller, whole |

## controller_set

Access: PAGE.

Set one field's value by its path (controller.group.field), checked against its type.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | required | controller.group.field |
| `value` | required | the new value, of the field's type |

## controller_remove

Access: PAGE.

Remove a controller from the workspace.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | required | the controller's id |

## controller_post

Access: PAGE.

Put one of the workspace's controllers in the project's feed, for the person to set. Use it when the work needs a decision that should hold for every piece from now on (a delivery spec, a caption style, who reviews what): a controller every agent reads. A decision about one piece of work is a note on that item, not a controller. Name the fields it's about (group.field, as controllers_read lists them) and say in a line what you need decided. A new controller is posted to the feed on its own; don't post it again.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `controller` | required | the controller's id |
| `fields` | optional | the fields to set, as group.field (or controller.group.field); the whole controller when left out |
| `why` | required | one line: what you need the person to decide, and why now |
| `title` | optional | what the person sees on the card; the controller's title when left out |

## channel_create

Access: PAGE.

Make a channel (a client, a game, a show) from one sentence on what it is. Returns its id.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `about` | required | one sentence on what the channel is |

## editor_selection

Access: PAGE.

What the person has open in the composition editor right now: the composition, its version file, the playhead (seconds), the part they picked in the frame (id, name, box as fractions of the frame, any unsaved move/scale), and how many unsaved changes there are. Read it when they say "this", "here" or "the selected one".

No input.

## editor_edit

Access: PAGE.

Change the composition open in the editor, the way the person does, in the version they're editing: it shows on their picture and their undo takes it back, and it's saved with their changes. Move, scale or fade a part on the picture (`part`: an id from editor_selection's parts; dx/dy in pixels, scale/opacity as multipliers), or move, trim, split or delete a <Sequence> on the timeline (`clip`: an i from editor_selection's clips; from/to/split in seconds, delete: true). One change a call. Read editor_selection first.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `part` | optional | a part id from editor_selection's parts |
| `dx` | optional | pixels right |
| `dy` | optional | pixels down |
| `scale` | optional | times its size now (1.2 = 20% bigger) |
| `opacity` | optional | times its opacity now |
| `clip` | optional | a clip's i from editor_selection's clips |
| `from` | optional | the clip's new start, seconds |
| `to` | optional | the clip's new end, seconds |
| `split` | optional | split the clip here, seconds |
| `delete` | optional | delete the clip |

## feed_items

Access: PAGE.

List the project's items, newest first: id, type, title, status, what each replaces, and the notes people left on it.

No input.

## whiteboard_read

Access: PAGE.

Read a whiteboard item: its plan (what you or another agent wrote) and every element on the board by id, with its text, the frame it's in, what an arrow joins, and by: plan or person (what people drew by hand).

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `board` | required | the whiteboard item's id |

## whiteboard_write

Access: PAGE.

Make a whiteboard (a plan, with no board) or change one (board plus a plan to replace its plan, or a patch). Say what is on it and how it's grouped; the feed lays it out, so never give positions. Sections become frames side by side: notes stacks cards, flow stacks them with arrows between, refs shows feed items' posters. People's own drawing on the board is kept.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `board` | optional | the whiteboard to change; leave out to make a new one |
| `plan` | optional | the whole board |
| `patch` | optional | changes by id to the board's plan |

## flow_board

Access: PAGE.

Put a ComfyUI workflow (UI or API format JSON, for example one a raea gen flow ran) on a whiteboard in the feed: each node a card with its settings, links as arrows, groups as frames, input and output images beside their nodes. The workflow is copied into the project and stays the source of truth.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `workflow` | required | absolute path of the workflow's .json on this machine |
| `title` | required | the board's title |

## flow_write

Access: PAGE.

Change a flow board's workflow (whiteboard_read shows its nodes and settings by name): settings' values, a node's mode (on, bypass, mute), and notes. The board is laid out again from it.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `board` | required | the flow board's item id |
| `widgets` | optional | settings to change |
| `modes` | optional | array |
| `notes` | optional | a Note node's new text, or a new note (no node) |

## flow_run

Access: PAGE.

Run a flow board's workflow as it stands through raea gen (ComfyUI). Its outputs go on the board and into the feed as look items, each a new version of the last run's.

| input | | |
|---|---|---|
| `board` | required | the flow board's item id |
